How much does it cost to run a soup maker?

A typical soup maker uses about 900 watts (800–1,000W depending on the model). Used for 25 minutes per use, 2 uses a week, it costs about 7.9p per use and £8.21 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per use
7.9p
About £8.21 a year at 25 minutes per use, 2 uses a week.

Standing charge not included.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Use the smallest appliance that does the job: a microwave or air fryer usually beats the oven for small portions.
  • Turn things off at the wall if they sit on standby all day.
  • Check the energy label when you replace an appliance; running costs over its life often outweigh the price difference.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a soup maker per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 900W model costs about 19p an hour, allowing for it running at full power about 80% of the time.

How much does it cost to run a soup maker per year?

About £8.21 a year, based on 25 minutes per use, 2 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my soup maker's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
